name: Cosmo First Ltd
title: Cosmo First Ltd - 508814 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Film utilisation 80-85% with 15-20% headroom, BOPP/BOPET spreads flat-to-up YoY but management flags 7-8 new Indian lines and BOPET oversupply; capex cycle done, net debt guided below 2x in 12-18 months.

capex.peers_comment: SRF may have decided to delay their CAPEX or defer their CAPEX at this stage.
capex.quote: CAPEX cycle of the Company is largely complete.

triggers.label: Seven to eight lines coming in India
triggers.quote: in the next three years, there are seven to eight lines coming in India

triggers.label: BOPP margin Rs 13 → Rs 20/kg QoQ
triggers.quote: BOPP margin was running at Rs 20/- per kg in Q4 vs Rs 13 per kg in Dec-25 quarter

triggers.label: BOPET anti-dumping duty on imports
triggers.quote: there is an anti-dumping duty on neighboring countries for BOPET film imports

triggers.label: Net debt to fall below 2x in 12-18 months
triggers.quote: We would like to bring this below 2x within 12 to 18 months from now.

guidance.quote: The Company expects double-digit topline growth next year
next year we expect it to be around 14% to 15% in the coming years
Cosmo Consumer business will have gross margins of anywhere between 35%-40%.
we are confident of the 50% CAGR itself in Cosmo Consumer as a minimum
We should see anywhere between 15 to 20% growth as a minimum in US business.
Given that next year the CAPEX is expected to be less than INR 100 crores.
in FY27, Plastech business should start making high single-digit EBITDA
EBITDA, we cannot talk about industry cycles, so it is always very difficult for us to give any guidance.

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated sales rose 37% to Rs 1,021 crore and EBITDA rose 53% to Rs 130 crore, with net debt cut to Rs 1,159 crore.
summary.overview: Cosmo First reported Q4 FY26 consolidated sales of Rs 1,021 crore (up 37% YoY on 41% volume growth) and EBITDA of Rs 130 crore (up 53% from Rs 85 crore), helped by new BOPP/CPP capacity, specialty volumes and a Rs 7 crore EBITDA rise at the specialty chemical subsidiary. PAT growth was moderate due to higher depreciation and interest, a Rs 7.2 crore exceptional provision at a Netherlands subsidiary and a Rs 5.3 crore deferred tax asset reversal in South Korea. For FY26, revenue rose 26% and EBITDA rose 32% to Rs 479 crore. Management said the capex cycle is largely complete, net debt fell Rs 75 crore over six months to Rs 1,159 crore, and it expects double-digit topline growth in FY27.

segments.name: BOPP/BOPET films
segments.commentary: BOPP margin about Rs 20/kg in Q4 vs Rs 13/kg in Dec-25 quarter; BOPET about Rs 18/kg vs Rs 12/kg in Dec-25 quarter. Films are about 90% BOPP-CPP and about 10% BOPET; specialty films are about 60% of films in Q4 (56-57% for full year).

segments.name: Specialty chemicals (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 sales Rs 54 crore with 25%+ EBITDA; FY26 sales Rs 204 crore. Value growth was about 10% because raw-material-linked pricing was lower, though volume grew about 20%.

segments.name: Cosmo Plastech (rigid packaging)
segments.commentary: Q4 topline up over 70% YoY; reached EBITDA breakeven in Q4 with a small PBT loss likely. FY26 turnover about Rs 92 crore. Management targets high single-digit EBITDA in FY27 and mid-to-high teens in FY28.

segments.name: Zigly (petcare)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 topline up 54% YoY; annualised run rate about Rs 90 crore. Plan to move it into a separate subsidiary in FY27, with possible external capital.

segments.name: Cosmo Consumer (window films, PPF, ceramic coatings)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 23 crore; exit annualised run rate about Rs 38 crore. Gross margin expected at 35-40%; still loss-making due to brand marketing. Management says at least two years to profitability and targets Rs 100 crore revenue first.

guidance_outlook: FY27 topline to grow in double digits, driven by utilisation of BOPP/CPP capacity added in FY26 and new businesses.
No EBITDA guidance given; management cited industry-cycle uncertainty but expects decent margins from new businesses, specialty growth and the US subsidiary.
Film volume growth potential of 15-20% from existing capacity; chemicals potential about Rs 100 crore more revenue; Plastech potential 30%; Cosmo Consumer at about 20% utilisation.
Capex for FY27 expected below Rs 100 crore; investment in Plastech, Consumer and Zigly about Rs 50-75 crore over next year and the year after.
Net debt to fall further; target to bring debt below 2x EBITDA within 12-18 months (currently 2.4x).
US tariff refund of more than Rs 60 crore expected over 6-12 months, partly payable back to customers; flows to both P&L and cash flow. Management expects Q1 FY27 to be better than Q4 FY26.
Operating cost (employee and other) expected to hold at Q4 run-rate plus inflation in FY27.
Dividend of Rs 4 per share recommended for FY26, subject to shareholder approval.
risks_watch: BOPP/BOPET spreads remain volatile as 7-8 new Indian BOPP lines arrive over three years; possible short-term core-film oversupply.
Speciality pricing lag (one to three months) can compress margins during raw material price swings.
Cosmo Consumer and Plastech still loss-making at PBT level; Cosmo Consumer will keep losing money in FY27 as marketing continues.
Net debt of Rs 1,159 crore (2.4x EBITDA) and potential interest-rate pressure from inflation; deleveraging target below 2x within 12-18 months.
Timing and size of US tariff refund (above Rs 60 crore, partly payable to customers) remains uncertain.
Management gave no quantitative EBITDA guidance and called the outlook highly uncertain.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 7.2 crore provision at Netherlands subsidiary
Rs 5.3 crore, South Korea subsidiary reorganisation

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 33 crore FY25; sales Rs 204 crore, 25%+ EBITDA margin
Down Rs 75 crore in last 6 months

qa_highlights.question: What is the industry outlook for BOPP and BOPET prices and spreads in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins may stay volatile as new capacity comes, though it sees a macro demand-supply balance. It said the company controls mix and cost, specialty films are 60% of films, and it is the lowest-cost producer in India.

qa_highlights.question: Is the employee and other cost base likely to keep rising after FY26 (employee expenses Rs 250 crore in FY25 vs Rs 336 crore in FY26)?
qa_highlights.answer: Costs should be held at the Q4 FY26 run rate plus normal inflation, and should fall as a percentage of sales as volumes grow.

qa_highlights.question: How much is the Plastech and Cosmo Consumer losses and when do they reach PBT break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Plastech reached EBITDA breakeven in Q4 with a possible small PBT loss; targets high single-digit EBITDA in FY27 and high-to-mid teens in FY28. Cosmo Consumer will keep losing money in FY27 due to marketing and needs at least two years to profitability.

qa_highlights.question: Why did specialty chemical growth slow to about 9-10% in FY26 against about 20% in prior years?
qa_highlights.answer: Value growth was about 10% because raw-material-linked prices were lower, while volume grew about 20%. EBITDA rose from Rs 33 crore to Rs 53 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 capacity utilisation across lines?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year utilisation is 80-85%, with 15-20% volume headroom in films, about Rs 100 crore revenue headroom in chemicals, 30% in Plastech and about 20% utilisation in Cosmo Consumer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt outlook and interest cost guidance amid possible rate hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt is expected to fall further, with FY27 capex below Rs 100 crore. Management aims to bring net debt/EBITDA below 2x within 12-18 months from 2.4x. It gave no interest-cost guidance.

capex_capacity: Film capacity: management cited 15-20% volume growth potential from existing BOPP/CPP capacity over last year's numbers; full-year FY26 utilisation of 80-85%.
Capex cycle described as largely complete; focus on sweating about Rs 1,200 crore of strategic capex made in the last three years.
FY27 capex expected to be below Rs 100 crore; investment in Plastech, Cosmo Consumer and Zigly about Rs 50-75 crore over the next year and the year after.
Capacity headroom in other businesses: specialty chemicals potential of about Rs 100 crore more revenue; Plastech potential growth of 30%; Cosmo Consumer at about 20% capacity utilisation.
Other businesses (Plastech, Cosmo Consumer, Zigly) have had about Rs 275-300 crore invested since inception, excluding films. Seven to eight new Indian BOPP lines expected over three years.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 BOPP margin about Rs 20/kg vs Rs 13/kg in Dec-25 quarter and Rs 20/kg in Mar-25 quarter; BOPET margin about Rs 18/kg vs Rs 12/kg in Dec-25 quarter and Rs 18/kg in Mar-25 quarter.
Management said BOPP spreads in April-May are broadly in the same range as Q4; BOPET spreads expected to rise per management trend view, with demand-supply balance in 12-18 months.
Indian flexible packaging volume growing 8-10%; BOPET demand growing 8-10% YoY with supply still slightly ahead of demand; anti-dumping duty on BOPET imports from neighbouring countries.
Specialty share of films about 60% in Q4 FY26 (down from ~70% before new BOPP line; 56-57% for full year); specialty volumes growing at about 10% CAGR.

Specialty chemicals value growth about 10% in FY26 as raw-material-linked pricing was lower, with volume growth about 20%; specialty gross margin per kg fell to Rs 63 from Rs 65 on a one-to-three-month pricing lag.
US business expected to grow at least 15-20%; US tariffs refund of more than Rs 60 crore, partly payable to customers, over 6-12 months.
Cosmo Consumer exit annualised run rate about Rs 38 crore vs FY26 revenue of Rs 23 crore; gross margin target 35-40%; management targets over 50% CAGR and Rs 100 crore revenue benchmark.
key_quotes: What we control is mix and cost.
We are also the lowest cost producer in India, which gives us downside protection.
We should see anywhere between 15 to 20% growth as a minimum in US business.
And we will bring it below within next 12 to 18 months.
summary.management_tone: Confident on specialty growth, Cosmo Consumer and US recovery, but cautious and explicitly non-committal on film spreads, EBITDA guidance and the operating environment, citing volatility and industry cycles.

adds.what: Seven to eight new Indian BOPP lines expected industry-wide over three years (industry supply, not company's own)

growth.why: Management expects double-digit FY27 topline growth (midpoint ~10%), backed by utilisation of BOPP/CPP capacity added in FY26 (utilisation 80-85%, 15-20% volume headroom), specialty growth and new businesses, but gave no EBITDA guidance and no specific new-capacity timing for the company itself.
